subject: Privatelink control-path degradation during quantized-agent upgrade — initial notification & follow-up
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-15T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Privatelink control-path degradation during quantized-agent upgrade — initial notification

Anita —

I wanted to reach out immediately with what we know so far and our first actions. At ~07:40 PST this morning we observed a spike of 502/504 errors for requests routed through your privatelink deployment. The traffic spike coincided with an automated rolling upgrade of the quantized-agent binary (v3.2.0-q). Between 07:40 and 08:05 PST your tenant saw intermittent control-path failures (API handshake errors and delayed connect attempts).

What we did first:
- Halted the upgrade and rolled back the quantized-agent to v3.1.7 at 07:52 PST.
- Deployed an emergency config that reverted a new kernel selection heuristic for quantized models.
- Repaired several agent registrations that had failed to rejoin after the canary.

Initial impact assessment:
- Duration: ~07:40–07:52 PST (service disruption window while upgrade was in progress) with residual retries until ~08:05 PST.
- Symptoms: transient API handshake failures, increased latency, a subset of requests returned 502.
- No evidence of data exfiltration; control plane requests are authenticated and we have no signs of unauthorized access. We will continue log-level analysis and can provide audit traces.

Next steps we are taking:
1) Full timeline + packet-level and auth logs for your tenant (ETA 24 hours).
2) Root cause analysis and postmortem draft (ETA 48 hours).
3) A tenant-specific canary policy we will propose for you to opt into that reduces parallel upgrade concurrency (we recommend that for private deployments).
4) Offer to schedule a bridge with our SRE and Deployment Engineering teams if you want a live walkthrough (I can set for today or tomorrow).

I'm very sorry for the disruption — we take private deployment stability seriously and will prioritize the postmortem and remediation. I've attached a preliminary incident timeline CSV and will follow up with a fuller write-up.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Privatelink control-path degradation during quantized-agent upgrade — initial notification

Markus —

Thanks for the quick note and the rollback. We saw a surge of errors across our staging and a couple of customer-facing services briefly lost connectivity; our on-call collected traces and I attached a short summary to this reply (see quoted excerpts below). Two things we'd like clarified up front:
1) Did any tenant secrets or model payloads traverse an unencrypted path during the incident?
2) How will we be compensated for SLA impact — we have an active contract that references availability for the privatelink control plane.

We appreciate the speedy rollback. We'd like to get the full timeline and a patch plan before we re-consider upgrades.

Date: 2027-01-15T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Privatelink control-path degradation — quick engineering notes for postmortem

Team —

Summary of what I heard from ops and the early RCA notes (please add/correct):
- Root cause: a kernel-selection heuristic introduced in quantized-agent v3.2.0-q selected a lower-latency path that unintentionally bypassed a short-lived KV-cache warming step. Under parallel upgrade concurrency the cache invalidations caused >100ms extra control-path latency and ~30% of handshakes to time out.
- Trigger: the rollout policy in our private deploy controller allowed 20% parallel rollout per rack for this customer; with multiple racks the overlap produced a high concurrent reconnect rate.
- Mitigation applied: rollback to v3.1.7 and reversion of the kernel-selection flag.
- Impact surface: control-plane operations (handshakes, registration). Data-plane inference requests that had an active session generally retried successfully; ephemeral requests during the window failed more often.

Action items (owners):
- Hiro: prepare a patch to the kernel-selection path that preserves KV warm-up under quantized code paths and include a unit test for reconnect scenarios. (ETA Wed 2027-01-20)
- Evelyn: propose a tenant-specific canary policy and low-parallel default for all private deployments; create feature flag to enforce 1-at-a-time per rack for critical customers. (ETA Mon 2027-01-18)
- Laura: draft customer-facing postmortem and credit recommendation; include timeline and proof of logs for AtlasHealth. (ETA 48 hours)
- Markus: coordinate bridge with AtlasHealth and confirm SLA credit process with Finance.

Please keep the timeline and packet logs internal until we confirm redactions for customer delivery. I'll assemble a first-pass postmortem and share with the thread.

-Markus

Date: 2027-01-16T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — Privatelink control-path degradation (Jan 15)

Anita / AtlasHealth Ops —

Thanks again for your patience. We've completed the internal RCA and prepared the attached postmortem and timeline for your review (postmortem-privatelink-20270116.md, incident-timeline-20270115.csv). Key points below:

Executive summary:
- What happened: during a rolling upgrade of the quantized-agent (v3.2.0-q) an optimization path skipped a necessary KV-cache warm-up under specific concurrency patterns, causing control-plane handshake timeouts for a subset of connections.
- Scope: your tenant experienced increased handshake failures between 07:40–07:52 PST on 2027-01-15; residual retries cleared by 08:05 PST.
- Impact to data: no evidence of unencrypted transfer or data exposure. All control-plane calls are authenticated; we are providing cryptographic audit traces in the attached logs.
- Root cause: regression in kernel-selection logic plus an overly permissive parallel rollout policy for private deployments.

Remediations completed:
1) Emergency rollback to v3.1.7 (07:52 PST).
2) Reverted the kernel-selection flag that caused the bypass.
3) Stabilized agent registrations and rebalanced the canary distribution.

Planned follow-ups and timeline:
- Patch (kernel-path + tests) staged; release candidate and canary expected by 2027-01-20.
- Tenant-specific canary policy: default to 1 agent per rack for critical private customers; rollout of policy to all customers in the next two weeks.
- SLA credits: Laura will follow up with a credit recommendation and calculation per our contract; Finance will confirm external issuance and timeline.

We want to propose a 30-minute bridge to walk through the postmortem and the proposed tenant-specific canary policy. Are you available tomorrow (Mon) between 09:00–12:00 PST, or would later in the week work better?

Again, apologies for the disruption — we appreciate the flag and the traces your team sent; they were helpful for reproducing the reconnect pattern in our lab. If you want more raw logs or packet captures for compliance review, we can provide them under NDA; let me know what you prefer.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
